words.enDefinition: period of the year marked by special events or activities in some field

examples.en: The mango season here lasts barely six weeks, and the whole town celebrates.
examples.zh: 这里的芒果「季节」只有短短六周，全镇都为此欢庆。

examples.en: My aunt waits for the rainy season to plant her chillies.
examples.zh: 姨妈总等雨「季」来了才下辣椒种。

words.enDefinition: anything (such as a document or a phonograph record or a photograph) providing permanent evidence of or information about past events

examples.en: Grandma's diary is a record of sixty years of market prices.
examples.zh: 外婆的日记是六十年市场物价的「记录」。

examples.en: The clinic keeps a record of every injection I've had since birth.
examples.zh: 诊所保存着我出生以来每次打针的「记录」。

words.enDefinition: someone who controls resources and expenditures

examples.en: The new school director visited every classroom in her first week.
examples.zh: 新上任的学校「主管」第一周就走遍了每间教室。

examples.en: Our community centre's director personally books the hall for festivals.
examples.zh: 社区中心的「主管」会亲自为节庆预订礼堂。

words.enDefinition: the day immediately before today

examples.en: Yesterday the market smelled of peaches; today it smells of rain.
examples.zh: 「昨天」市场里满是桃子的香气，今天却是一股雨味。

examples.en: I mailed the parcel yesterday, so it should reach Auntie by Friday.
examples.zh: 「昨天」我把包裹寄出去了，周五前应该能到姨妈家。

words.enDefinition: change resulting in an increase

examples.en: A ten percent increase in rent pushed us to the cheaper street.
examples.zh: 房租「上涨」一成，逼得我们搬去了便宜的那条街。

examples.en: The bakery noticed an increase in customers after the radio mention.
examples.zh: 电台提到之后，面包店的顾客明显「增加」了。

words.enDefinition: a lid or other object placed over something to close or protect it

examples.en: The pan's glass cover lets me watch the soup without lifting anything.
examples.zh: 锅上的玻璃「盖子」让我不用掀开就能看着汤。

examples.en: A plastic cover over the bike seat keeps the rain off.
examples.zh: 车座上罩个塑料「盖」能挡雨。

words.enDefinition: worker who holds or is invested with an office

examples.en: The city official measured our flooded street twice and promised a drain.
examples.zh: 市里来的「官员」把被淹的街道量了两遍，承诺增设排水口。

examples.en: A customs official opened our suitcase at the border and laughed at the noodles.
examples.zh: 边境的海关「官员」打开我们的行李箱，看着里面的面条笑了。

words.enDefinition: the body of faculty and students at a university

examples.en: My sister's university sits ten minutes from the sea, which she chose first.
examples.zh: 姐姐的「大学」离海边十分钟路程，这是她选校的首要理由。

examples.en: The university gates open to townspeople every Sunday for the orchard walk.
examples.zh: 每周日「大学」的校门向镇民开放，供大家进果园散步。

words.enDefinition: 16 ounces avoirdupois

examples.en: The recipe asks for half a pound of butter, which startled my metric scales.
examples.zh: 食谱要半「磅」黄油，我的公制秤一时不知所措。

examples.en: At the market, a pound of tomatoes costs less than one coffee downtown.
examples.zh: 在市场买一「磅」番茄，比市中心一杯咖啡还便宜。

words.enDefinition: a person who holds a position of authority in an organisation, government, or the armed forces

examples.en: The admissions officer called my mother by her full name, which charmed her.
examples.zh: 招生「干事」连名带姓地称呼我妈，把她逗乐了。

examples.en: A customs officer waved our van through after one glance at the lanterns.
examples.zh: 海关「官员」瞥了一眼车上的灯笼，就挥手放行了我们的面包车。

words.enDefinition: only one; not married or not in a romantic relationship

examples.en: Everyone at the reunion asked why I was still single, then ate my snacks.
examples.zh: 聚会所有人都在问我为什么还「单身」，然后吃光了我的零食。

examples.en: A single umbrella stood by the door, nobody claimed it.
examples.zh: 门边立着一把「孤零零的」伞，没人认领。

words.enDefinition: the reflexive or emphatic form of she/her

examples.en: Grandma replanted the balcony by herself, refusing all offers of help.
examples.zh: 外婆坚持「自己」动手，一个人重新栽种了阳台的花，谁帮忙都不要。

examples.en: She caught herself laughing at her own joke halfway through.
examples.zh: 讲到一半，她连「自己」都被自己的笑话逗笑了。

words.enDefinition: an opportunity to do something; a possibility that something will happen

examples.en: There's a chance the ferry still runs if the storm passes by noon.
examples.zh: 如果风暴中午前过去，「说不定」轮渡还会开。

examples.en: I took the chance to ask the baker for the burnt loaf at half price.
examples.zh: 我趁机「抓住机会」，向面包师提议把烤糊的面包半价卖给我。

words.enDefinition: male with the same parents as someone else

examples.en: My brother taught me to swim by letting go a little further each lesson.
examples.zh: 「哥哥」教我游泳的办法是每次松手远一点点。

examples.en: Her brother paints the shop sign anew every spring festival.
examples.zh: 她的「兄弟」每年春节都把店招牌重新刷一遍。

words.enDefinition: the way a machine, system, or organisation works; also a surgical procedure

examples.en: The whole bakery operation runs on two ovens and one stubborn alarm clock.
examples.zh: 整个面包坊的「运营」全靠两台烤箱和一个固执的闹钟。

examples.en: Grandpa's knee operation was scheduled right after the autumn harvest.
examples.zh: 爷爷的膝盖「手术」安排在秋收一结束就做。

words.enDefinition: a living organism such as a tree, flower, or grass that typically grows in soil

examples.en: The new plant on my desk needs weekly watering and monthly praise.
examples.zh: 书桌上这盆新「植物」每周浇一次水，每月还要夸一夸。

examples.en: Every plant on the windowsill leans toward the same pane of glass.
examples.zh: 窗台上的每盆「植物」都朝同一块玻璃倾斜。

words.enDefinition: female human offspring

examples.en: Their daughter runs the family noodle shop better than either parent.
examples.zh: 他们的「女儿」把家里的面馆经营得比父母任何一方都好。

examples.en: My daughter calls from the market asking how much fish is too much fish.
examples.zh: 「女儿」从市场打来电话，问我买多少鱼才算买多了。

words.enDefinition: vote to select the winner of a position or political office

examples.en: The village election turned the market square into a debate hall for a week.
examples.zh: 村里的「选举」让市场广场变成了一周的辩论场。

examples.en: During the election, every lamppost wore a poster by Friday.
examples.zh: 「选举」期间，到周五每根灯杆都贴上了海报。

words.enDefinition: the time yet to come

examples.en: Saving twenty yuan a month feels small until the future asks for it.
examples.zh: 每月存二十块看着不起眼，直到「未来」开口要用。

examples.en: She plans her future around one spreadsheet and two rainy-day funds.
examples.zh: 她用一张表格和两笔应急金规划「未来」。

words.enDefinition: a planned series of actions intended to achieve a particular goal, in war, politics, or marketing

examples.en: The poster campaign against littering covered every bin in the district.
examples.zh: 反对乱丢垃圾的「宣传运动」覆盖了全区每个垃圾桶。

examples.en: Our class campaign for longer library hours gathered two hundred signatures.
examples.zh: 我们班争取延长图书馆开放时间的「活动」收集了两百个签名。

words.enDefinition: the property of an object that is perceived as red, blue, green, etc.; also UK spelling of color

examples.en: The wall changes colour between the morning sun and the evening lamp.
examples.zh: 这面墙在朝阳和夜灯下会呈现不同的「颜色」。

examples.en: Choose a paint colour you can live with for ten years, Dad advised.
examples.zh: 爸爸建议，选「颜色」要选能忍受十年的。

words.enDefinition: a flow of electricity, water, or air; also the present period of time when used as an adjective in other senses

examples.en: The river's current pulls leaves downstream faster than the ducks swim.
examples.zh: 河里的「水流」把落叶冲向下游，比鸭子游得还快。

examples.en: Check the current before swimming; the estuary looks calm and isn't.
examples.zh: 下水前先看「水流」，河口看着平静，其实不然。

words.enDefinition: a formal accusation that someone has committed an offence; also an amount of money asked for a service

examples.en: The repair shop added a mystery charge that turned out to be cleaning.
examples.zh: 修理店收了一笔莫名的「费用」，原来只是清洁费。

examples.en: The dropped charge against my neighbour came with an apology letter.
examples.zh: 对邻居的「指控」撤销了，还附了一封道歉信。

words.enDefinition: the act of fighting; any contest or struggle

examples.en: The fight over the last parking spot lasted four minutes and two reverse gears.
examples.zh: 为了最后一个车位的「争夺」持续了四分钟、倒了两次车。

examples.en: The brothers' fight over the TV remote is a nightly tradition.
examples.zh: 兄弟俩抢电视遥控器的「斗争」是每晚的保留节目。

words.enDefinition: the act of working out the form of something (as by making a sketch or outline or plan)

examples.en: The bakery's design mixes a village counter with a city glass wall.
examples.zh: 这家面包店的「设计」把乡村柜台和城市的玻璃墙混搭在一起。

examples.en: She copied the paper lantern's design for her woodwork homework.
examples.zh: 她照着纸灯笼的「样式」完成了木工课作业。

words.enDefinition: physical force against a surface; also stress caused by demands or difficulties

examples.en: A cool cloth eased the pressure in Grandma's head, with no questions asked.
examples.zh: 外婆头部的「压力」，靠一条凉毛巾就能缓解，外加不许多问。

examples.en: The pressure in my ears eased once we left the tunnel.
examples.zh: 出了隧道，我耳朵的「压迫感」就缓解了。

words.enDefinition: something that interests you because it is important or affects you

examples.en: My main concern was the leaking roof, not the peeling paint.
examples.zh: 我最「担心的事」是屋顶漏水，而不是墙皮剥落。

examples.en: She voiced her concern about the long walk home after dark.
examples.zh: 她说出了自己对天黑后走长路的「担忧」。

words.enDefinition: an urgent or peremptory request

examples.en: His demand for a window seat emptied the whole negotiation table.
examples.zh: 他非要靠窗座位不可的「要求」让整桌谈判不欢而散。

examples.en: The tenants' list of demands reached the landlord's desk on Monday.
examples.zh: 租客们的「要求清单」周一就摆上了房东的桌面。

words.enDefinition: social class comprising those who do manual labor or work for wages

examples.en: Harvesting the paddy took three weeks of labour and one borrowed tractor.
examples.zh: 收割水稻花了三周「劳动」和一台借来的拖拉机。

examples.en: The brick kiln relied on migrant labour every dry season.
examples.zh: 砖窑每年旱季都依赖外来「劳工」。

words.enDefinition: assets available for use in the production of further assets

examples.en: Her cousin lent starting capital for the noodle cart, interest-free.
examples.zh: 她表哥为那辆面摊车提供了免息「启动资金」。

examples.en: Without capital, the print shop stayed a plan in a notebook.
examples.zh: 没有「资金」，那家打印店始终只是笔记本里的一个计划。

words.enDefinition: earnest and conscientious activity intended to do or accomplish something

examples.en: My first attempt at sourdough fed the birds instead of the family.
examples.zh: 我第一次「尝试」做酸面包，成果喂了鸟而不是家人。

examples.en: Each attempt at the driving test cost him a week of practice.
examples.zh: 每次「尝试」考驾照，他都要先练上一周。

words.enDefinition: concerned with work or important matters rather than play or trivialities

examples.en: Dad turned serious the very moment the medical report opened.
examples.zh: 医疗报告一翻开，爸爸立刻「严肃」了起来。

examples.en: Our club wants serious members, not ones who vanish after the first hike.
examples.zh: 社团要的是「认真」的成员，而不是第一次远足后就消失的人。

words.enDefinition: statement (either spoken or written) that is made to reply to a question or request or criticism or accusation

examples.en: Nobody could remember the answer until the smallest cousin whispered it.
examples.zh: 没人记得「答案」，直到年纪最小的表弟悄悄说出。

examples.en: Her answer to the tricky question was to offer everyone tea.
examples.zh: 面对刁钻的问题，她的「回应」是请大家喝茶。

words.enDefinition: the final match between the winners of all previous matches in an elimination tournament

examples.en: Grandpa fell asleep before the final ended and blamed the ref.
examples.zh: 「决赛」还没结束爷爷就睡着了，还怪裁判。

examples.en: The badminton final drew the whole lane to one courtyard screen.
examples.zh: 羽毛球「决赛」把整条巷子的人都聚到了一块大屏前。

words.enDefinition: (military) an offensive against an enemy (using weapons)

examples.en: The paper described the editorial as a personal attack, not criticism.
examples.zh: 报纸称那篇社论是人身「攻击」，而非批评。

examples.en: My bold chess attack collapsed the moment he traded queens.
examples.zh: 他一换后，我的棋局「攻势」就崩了。

words.enDefinition: make known; make an announcement

examples.en: Grandma announced the engagement before the couple even finished eating.
examples.zh: 小两口还没吃完，外婆就「宣布」了订婚的消息。

examples.en: The principal announced the snow day over the crackling loudspeaker.
examples.zh: 校长通过沙沙作响的喇叭「宣布」了雪假。

words.enDefinition: the region that is outside of something

examples.en: The dog waited outside the bakery every day at closing time.
examples.zh: 那只狗每天打烊时分都在面包店「外面」等着。

examples.en: Leave the wet boots outside, or the hallway smells all week.
examples.zh: 湿靴子放「门外」，不然楼道一整周都有味儿。

words.enDefinition: female person who has the same parents as another person

examples.en: My sister navigates night markets better than any phone map.
examples.zh: 我「姐姐」逛夜市比任何手机地图都靠谱。

examples.en: Her sister sends postcards from small towns nobody can pronounce.
examples.zh: 她「妹妹」从名字都念不顺的小镇寄来明信片。

words.enDefinition: counting everything together; complete with nothing left out

examples.en: The total bill came to less than the two of us feared.
examples.zh: 「总共」的账单比我们俩担心的要少。

examples.en: After the total power cut, the whole lane cooked on one stove.
examples.zh: 彻底断电后，「整条巷子」的人都在一个炉子上做饭。

words.enDefinition: the sound of laughing

examples.en: A laugh from the kitchen told us the cake had collapsed.
examples.zh: 厨房传来一声「大笑」，我们就知道蛋糕塌了。

examples.en: Her loud laugh carries two tables away in the teahouse.
examples.zh: 在茶馆里，她的「笑声」隔着两张桌子都能听见。

words.enDefinition: the act of going to see some person or place or thing for a short time

examples.en: The family visit stretched from lunch until the last bus.
examples.zh: 这次家庭「拜访」从中午一直持续到末班车时间。

examples.en: A quick visit to the dentist turned into two fillings.
examples.zh: 一次「看牙」的小拜访，变成了补两颗牙。

words.enDefinition: green color or pigment; resembling the color of growing grass

examples.en: The door turned green before my aunt lost interest in housework.
examples.zh: 门被刷成「绿色」后不久，姨妈就对家务失去了兴趣。

examples.en: The green shutters made the grey house look newly built.
examples.zh: 「绿色」的百叶窗让灰扑扑的房子像新盖的一样。

words.enDefinition: a device for receiving radio broadcasts; radio as a medium of communication

examples.en: Grandpa fixes the old radio every spring and tunes it to the opera station.
examples.zh: 外公每年春天都修一修那台旧「收音机」，调到戏曲台。

examples.en: The news reached our village by radio long before any newspaper.
examples.zh: 消息通过「无线电广播」传到我们村，比任何报纸都早。

words.enDefinition: the state prevailing during the absence of war

examples.en: The ceasefire held, and the village slept in peace for the first night in months.
examples.zh: 停火生效后，村里几个月来头一回在「和平」中入睡。

examples.en: Grandpa guards his peace by fishing alone before sunrise, always.
examples.zh: 外公靠日出前独自钓鱼守着自己的「安宁」。

words.enDefinition: straight or straightforward, without stops, bends, or detours

examples.en: The direct bus to campus skips the market and saves fifteen minutes.
examples.zh: 「直达」校区的公交不绕市场，省下十五分钟。

examples.en: Give me a direct answer: is the rent going up or not?
examples.zh: 给我一个「直截了当的」回答：房租到底涨不涨？

words.enDefinition: the print media responsible for gathering and publishing news in the form of newspapers or magazines

examples.en: The local press photographed the flooded underpass before the council arrived.
examples.zh: 议会的人还没到，「新闻界」就把被淹的地下通道拍了个遍。

examples.en: Grandma trusts the village press more than any city channel.
examples.zh: 比起城市频道，外婆更信村里的「媒体」。

words.enDefinition: direct or control; projects, businesses, etc.

examples.en: My aunt and uncle operate the corner shop in alternating shifts.
examples.zh: 姨妈和姨夫轮班「经营」街角小店。

examples.en: Who exactly operates the ferry during the storm season, though?
examples.zh: 风暴季是谁在「运营」渡轮？

words.enDefinition: an intermediate part or section

examples.en: Grandma plants mint in the middle of the vegetable patch.
examples.zh: 外婆把薄荷种在菜地「中央」。

examples.en: The bench sits in the middle of the market, always crowded.
examples.zh: 那张长椅在市场「正中」，总是挤满了人。

words.enDefinition: having all necessary parts; finished or total

examples.en: The jigsaw lay complete on the table for exactly one hour.
examples.zh: 拼图「完整」地在桌上摆了整整一个小时。

examples.en: The collection is complete once the last stamp arrives from Dalian.
examples.zh: 等大连的最后一枚邮票寄到，这套收藏就「齐」了。

words.enDefinition: free from external control and constraint

examples.en: The ferry keeps running in the storm; it's stubbornly independent.
examples.zh: 风暴天渡轮照常运行，倔强得很「独立」。

examples.en: Grandma has been financially independent since she opened the stall at forty.
examples.zh: 外婆四十岁摆摊起，经济上就「独立」了。

words.enDefinition: the side that is forward or prominent

examples.en: The bakery's front window always shows tomorrow's celebration cakes first.
examples.zh: 面包店的「前面」橱窗最先摆出明天的蛋糕。

examples.en: Sit at the front of the bus if you want to feel every pothole.
examples.zh: 想感受每一个坑洼，就坐公交车「前排」。

words.enDefinition: lighter consisting of a thin piece of wood or cardboard tipped with combustible chemical; ignites with friction

examples.en: The camp stove refused to light until the third match.
examples.zh: 直到第三根「火柴」，炉子才点着。

examples.en: Grandpa lights his pipe with a single wooden match and one long breath.
examples.zh: 外公只用一根木「火柴」和一口长气点烟斗。

words.enDefinition: merchandise issued for sale or public showing (especially a record or film)

examples.en: The album's release date slipped twice, then arrived on my birthday.
examples.zh: 专辑的「发行」日期推迟了两次，最后落在我生日那天。

examples.en: The film's long-awaited release drew queues around the old cinema.
examples.zh: 影片「上映」让老影院门口排起了长队。

words.enDefinition: most important element

examples.en: The fire chief inspected every one of our lane's extinguishers himself.
examples.zh: 消防「队长」亲自检查了我们巷子的灭火器。

examples.en: As chief of the volunteer brigade, Auntie Mei assigns the night shifts.
examples.zh: 梅姨是志愿消防队的「头儿」，负责排夜班。

words.enDefinition: done or taking place in a short time; moving fast

examples.en: A quick breakfast of buns and tea got me to the exam on time.
examples.zh: 包子加茶的一份「快手」早餐让我赶上了考试。

examples.en: She gave the draft a quick read and found three typos.
examples.zh: 她把草稿「快速」读了一遍，揪出三个错别字。

words.enDefinition: the astonishment you feel when something totally unexpected happens to you

examples.en: The surprise wasn't the cake; it was Grandma pretending to be shocked.
examples.zh: 「惊喜」不是蛋糕，而是外婆假装吓了一跳的样子。

examples.en: Snow in April was a surprise the farmers did not welcome.
examples.zh: 四月下雪，这份「意外」农民们可不欢迎。

words.enDefinition: an orange of low brightness and saturation

examples.en: The dog's brown ears flop differently when it is happy.
examples.zh: 狗「棕色」的耳朵一高兴就摆出不一样的弧度。

examples.en: We painted the fence brown to hide the rain stains.
examples.zh: 我们把栅栏刷成「褐色」，好遮住雨水留下的印子。

words.enDefinition: hypothetical description of a complex entity or process

examples.en: Grandpa built a scale model of our street for the heritage fair.
examples.zh: 外公为民俗展搭了一条我们这条街的「模型」。

examples.en: The airplane model on his shelf took two winters to finish.
examples.zh: 他架子上的飞机「模型」花了两个冬天才完成。

words.enDefinition: someone who controls resources and expenditures

examples.en: The friendly night-shift manager knows every regular's order by heart.
examples.zh: 夜班「经理」熟记每位常客的点单。

examples.en: Our building's manager chases the lift repairman better than anyone.
examples.zh: 我们楼的「管理员」追起电梯修理工来比谁都勤。

words.enDefinition: planned undertaking

examples.en: Our street's mural project took one summer and forty buckets of paint.
examples.zh: 我们这条街的壁画「项目」用了一个夏天和四十桶颜料。

examples.en: The rooftop garden project began with three buckets and one argument.
examples.zh: 屋顶花园「计划」始于三只桶和一场争论。

words.enDefinition: to a distinctly greater extent or degree than is common

examples.en: Grandma saves the chicken wing tips especially for the soup.
examples.zh: 外婆「特意」把鸡翅尖留起来煲汤。

examples.en: The stall sells out early, especially on rainy market days.
examples.zh: 雨天赶集时，摊位总是早早卖完，「尤其」抢手。

words.enDefinition: framework of wood or metal that contains a glass windowpane and is built into a wall or roof to admit light or air

examples.en: The kitchen window frames the market exactly like a slow film.
examples.zh: 厨房「窗户」框出的市场景象宛如一部慢镜头电影。

examples.en: Rain taps the bedroom window all night in typhoon season.
examples.zh: 台风季，雨点整夜敲打着卧室「窗」。

words.enDefinition: the unlimited expanse in which everything is located

examples.en: There's barely space for one more chair in this study room.
examples.zh: 这间书房几乎没有「空间」再放一把椅子。

examples.en: The van filled up, and we found space for the bicycle on the roof.
examples.zh: 面包车装满了，我们在车顶找到了放自行车的「空位」。

words.enDefinition: be pertinent or relevant or applicable

examples.en: The generous student discount applies only on weekdays before noon.
examples.zh: 学生「折扣」只在工作日中午前「适用」。

examples.en: The same rule applies to the library and the computer lab.
examples.zh: 这条规定在图书馆和机房同样「适用」。

words.enDefinition: under normal conditions

examples.en: I usually miss the first bus and walk past the morning market instead.
examples.zh: 我「通常」会错过头班车，改为步行穿过早市。

examples.en: Grandpa usually waters the plants before the sun reaches the balcony.
examples.zh: 外公「通常」赶在太阳照到阳台之前浇花。

words.enDefinition: Everybody; -- commonly separated, every one.

examples.en: Everyone on our floor chips in for the cleaner's festival gift.
examples.zh: 我们这层楼「每个人」都凑份子给保洁阿姨买节日礼物。

examples.en: Everyone laughed when the parrot recited the professor's opening line.
examples.zh: 鹦鹉背出教授的开场白时，「大家」都笑了。

words.enDefinition: pair who associate with one another

examples.en: The elderly couple shares one umbrella and argues over the pace.
examples.zh: 这对老「夫妇」合撑一把伞，还要争谁走得太快。

examples.en: A young couple occupied the corner table since before we queued.
examples.zh: 那对年轻「情侣」从我们排队前就占着角落那桌。

words.enDefinition: in truth (often tends to intensify)

examples.en: The soup was, indeed, well worth the two-block morning queue.
examples.zh: 这碗汤「的确」值得排两条街的队。

examples.en: Grandpa said the frost would come early, and indeed it did.
examples.zh: 外公说霜期会提前，「果然」应验了。

words.enDefinition: an essential and distinguishing attribute of something or someone

examples.en: The tailor judges quality by the seams, not the label.
examples.zh: 裁缝看衣服「品质」只看针脚，不看商标。

examples.en: Market tomatoes beat supermarket ones on quality and taste every summer.
examples.zh: 每年夏天，市场番茄的「品质」都胜过超市货。

words.enDefinition: definitely or positively (`sure' is sometimes used informally for `surely')

examples.en: You may certainly borrow the tent; just dry it afterwards.
examples.zh: 你「当然」可以借帐篷，只要之后晾干就行。

examples.en: The recipe will certainly fail if you skip the resting step.
examples.zh: 省掉醒面那一步，这道食谱「肯定」会失败。

words.enDefinition: marked by correspondence or resemblance

examples.en: The two rooftop gardens look similar, but one grows chilies secretly.
examples.zh: 两个屋顶花园看着「相似」，其中一个却偷偷种了辣椒。

examples.en: My handwriting is quite similar to Dad's, except on envelopes.
examples.zh: 我的字和爸爸的「很像」，写信封时除外。

words.enDefinition: to give instruction or help someone learn

examples.en: Grandma taught me to fold dumplings faster than any video could.
examples.zh: 外婆「教」我包饺子，比任何视频都快。

examples.en: The retired captain offered to teach rowing to the younger scouts.
examples.zh: 退役船长主动提出教年轻童子军「划船」。

words.enDefinition: an iconic mental representation

examples.en: The temple's image of the guardian was repainted every spring.
examples.zh: 寺庙里守护神「像」每年春天都要重新描漆。

examples.en: My first mental image of the city came from Grandma's stories.
examples.zh: 我对这座城市的最初「印象」来自外婆的故事。

words.enDefinition: absolutely essential

examples.en: Grandma says sunscreen is necessary even on cloudy beach days.
examples.zh: 即使是阴天的海滩，防晒霜也是「必要的」。

examples.en: It wasn't necessary to bring the whole toolbox to fix one chair.
examples.zh: 修一把椅子带整套工具箱，实在「没有必要」。

words.enDefinition: thing constructed; a complex entity constructed of many parts

examples.en: The old bridge's stone structure survived three floods this century.
examples.zh: 老桥的石头「结构」扛过了本世纪三次洪水。

examples.en: The essay needs a clearer structure: one idea per paragraph.
examples.zh: 这篇文章「结构」需要更清晰：一段只讲一件事。

words.enDefinition: a device used to make and receive calls; a telephone

examples.en: My poor phone survives almost everything except Grandpa's pocket sand.
examples.zh: 我的「手机」什么都扛得住，除了外公口袋里的沙子。

examples.en: The shop fixed my phone screen while I ate two dumplings.
examples.zh: 趁我吃两个饺子的工夫，店里就修好了「手机」屏幕。

words.enDefinition: to have something inside or as a part of something larger

examples.en: The welcome pack contains maps, keys, and one suspicious cookie.
examples.zh: 迎宾包里「装着」地图、钥匙，还有一块可疑的饼干。

examples.en: Grandma's soup contains nothing that is written in any recipe book.
examples.zh: 外婆的汤里「含」的东西哪本菜谱都找不到。

words.enDefinition: visual representation (of an object or scene or person or abstraction) produced on a surface

examples.en: The framed picture above the fireplace is older than the house.
examples.zh: 壁炉上方那幅「画」比房子年头还久。

examples.en: She drew a picture of the courtyard from the balcony every evening.
examples.zh: 她每晚都在阳台上画一幅院子的「画」。

words.enDefinition: separate part of a whole

examples.en: A single piece of chocolate ends every argument in our house.
examples.zh: 在我们家，一块「巧克力」能终结所有争执。

examples.en: The vase broke into five pieces; the cat looked innocent.
examples.zh: 花瓶碎成五「块」，猫一脸无辜。

words.enDefinition: an isolated fact that is considered separately from the whole

examples.en: The tailor noticed every detail, down to the mismatched buttons.
examples.zh: 裁缝注意到每个「细节」，连不配对的纽扣都不放过。

examples.en: Check the bus detail on the ticket before you leave tonight.
examples.zh: 今晚出门前，先核对票上的「细节」信息。

words.enDefinition: cut down on; make a reduction in

examples.en: Cycling to the market reduced my spending and my patience for parking.
examples.zh: 骑车去市场「减少」了开销，也「减掉」了我找车位的耐心。

examples.en: Grandpa reduced his coffee to one cup after the doctor's talk.
examples.zh: 医生谈话后，外公把咖啡「减」到了一天一杯。

words.enDefinition: absolutely; altogether; really

examples.en: The repair was simply a loose screw after all that worry.
examples.zh: 白担心一场，问题「只是」一颗松掉的螺丝。

examples.en: That new noodle place is simply too crowded to enjoy.
examples.zh: 那家新面馆「简直」挤得没法好好吃。

words.enDefinition: licensed medical practitioner

examples.en: The doctor replaced my grandfather's handwritten notes with a printed list.
examples.zh: 「医生」把外公手写的用药单换成了打印版。

examples.en: Our family doctor remembers birthdays better than my phone does.
examples.zh: 家庭「医生」记生日比我的手机还牢。

words.enDefinition: form of entertainment that enacts a story by sound and a sequence of images giving the illusion of continuous movement

examples.en: The open-air movie started an hour late because of the rain.
examples.zh: 露天「电影」因为下雨晚开了一小时。

examples.en: Grandma narrates every movie, five minutes ahead of the plot.
examples.zh: 外婆给每部「电影」都配解说，还总比剧情快五分钟。

words.enDefinition: set up or found

examples.en: The night market established itself on our street in a single spring.
examples.zh: 夜市只用了一个春天就在我们这条街「立足」。

examples.en: The scholarship established by Auntie Mei's class still funds two students.
examples.zh: 梅姨班级设立的「奖学金」至今还资助着两名学生。

words.enDefinition: machine for performing calculations automatically

examples.en: The library computer still runs the card catalogue faster than my laptop.
examples.zh: 图书馆的「电脑」查卡片目录比我的笔记本还快。

examples.en: Grandpa's computer plays chess and nothing else, by his choice.
examples.zh: 外公的「电脑」只下棋，别的都不装，这是他的选择。

words.enDefinition: belonging to or for the use of one particular person or group only

examples.en: The rooftop is private, so our drying racks stay untouched.
examples.zh: 屋顶是「私人的」，我们的晾衣架从没人动。

examples.en: Keep the gate locked at night; the courtyard is private property.
examples.zh: 把门锁好，院子是「私人」地方。

words.enDefinition: ideas or actions intended to deal with a problem or situation

examples.en: Her approach to stubborn stains starts with an overnight soak.
examples.zh: 她对付顽固污渍的「方法」是先泡一夜。

examples.en: The young teacher's calm approach turned the noisiest class around.
examples.zh: 老师平和的「方式」让最吵闹的班都变了样。

words.enDefinition: the relative magnitude of something with reference to a criterion

examples.en: A small amount of chili oil goes a long way in this soup.
examples.zh: 这汤里放「少量」的辣椒油就够劲了。

examples.en: Count the exact amount twice before handing over the rent.
examples.zh: 交房租前把「数目」点两遍。

words.enDefinition: drawback or difficulty that is not readily evident

examples.en: The offer sounded perfect, so naturally we hunted for the catch.
examples.zh: 优惠听起来完美，我们自然开始找「蹊跷」。

examples.en: There's always a catch: the free gym trial ends with a hard sell.
examples.zh: 总有「陷阱」：免费健身体验的最后是硬推销。

words.enDefinition: an elaborate and systematic plan of action

examples.en: The council's new scheme pairs empty nesters with student tenants.
examples.zh: 议会的「方案」让空巢老人和学生租客结对。

examples.en: Under the new recycling scheme, our lane separates three bins.
examples.zh: 按新的回收「计划」，我们巷子要分三个桶。

words.enDefinition: grant made by a law court

examples.en: The court's award covered the repairs to our crushed fence.
examples.zh: 法院的「判给金」覆盖了被撞坏篱笆的修理费。

examples.en: Her lawyer explained how the award would be paid in instalments.
examples.zh: 律师解释了「裁定赔偿额」将如何分期支付。

words.enDefinition: the process whereby a person concentrates on some features of the environment to the (relative) exclusion of others

examples.en: Grandpa's attention drifts away unless the radio mentions the weather.
examples.zh: 只要广播不提天气，外公的「注意力」就会飘走。

examples.en: Pay attention when the recipe says add eggs one at a time.
examples.zh: 菜谱说鸡蛋要一个个加时，「注意」照做。

words.enDefinition: to succeed in doing or getting what you wanted, usually after effort

examples.en: Grandma achieved her goal of reading the whole newspaper daily.
examples.zh: 外婆「实现」了每天读完整份报纸的目标。

examples.en: The team achieved a full house for the first night market.
examples.zh: 团队让首届夜市「办到」了满场。

words.enDefinition: subdivision of a written work; usually numbered and titled

examples.en: Chapter three patiently explains why Grandma salts the eggplant twice.
examples.zh: 「第三章」解释了外婆为什么要给茄子撒两次盐。

examples.en: I read one chapter of the mystery each night, like medicine.
examples.zh: 每晚读「一章」那本悬疑小说，像吃药一样定时。

words.enDefinition: pick out, select, or choose from a number of alternatives

examples.en: Grandma lets me choose the fruit; I always pick loquats.
examples.zh: 外婆让我来「挑」水果，我总选枇杷。

examples.en: We chose the slower boat because it allowed deck picnics.
examples.zh: 我们「选」了慢船，因为甲板上可以野餐。

words.enDefinition: something owned; any tangible or intangible possession that is owned by someone;

examples.en: Grandma's most treasured piece of property is a keyring, oddly.
examples.zh: 说来奇怪，外婆最珍视的「财产」是一个钥匙圈。

examples.en: The rental property on the corner changes tenants every May.
examples.zh: 街角那处出租「房产」每年五月都换租客。

words.enDefinition: document (or organization) from which information is obtained

examples.en: The recipe's true source was Grandma's church cookbook from 1978.
examples.zh: 这道菜的「出处」是外婆 1978 年的教会食谱。

examples.en: Cite the source under every photo, the teacher reminded us.
examples.zh: 老师提醒我们，每张照片下面都要标「来源」。

words.enDefinition: (of actions or states) slightly short of or not quite accomplished; all but

examples.en: The dumplings were nearly gone by the time I reached the table.
examples.zh: 等我走到桌边，饺子「几乎」没了。

examples.en: Grandpa nearly won the chess match until his phone rang.
examples.zh: 外公的棋「差点」就赢了，这时他的手机响了。

words.enDefinition: the direction where the sun sets; the southern part of a place

examples.en: We drove south until the smell of the sea replaced the market's.
examples.zh: 我们一路向「南」开，直到海风替代了市场的气味。

examples.en: The south side of the house catches the afternoon sun.
examples.zh: 房子「朝南」的一面晒得到午后阳光。

words.enDefinition: hear with intention

examples.en: Grandpa listens to the opera channel while shelling beans outside.
examples.zh: 外公一边剥豆子一边「听」戏曲频道。

examples.en: Listen to the kettle carefully; it sings before it boils.
examples.zh: 「听」水壶的声音，它会在烧开前先唱歌。

words.enDefinition: particular society at a particular time and place

examples.en: Our lane's dumpling culture has survived three generations of change.
examples.zh: 我们这条巷子的饺子「文化」传了三代人。

examples.en: The exchange student taught us tea culture from her province.
examples.zh: 交换生给我们讲了她家乡的茶「文化」。

words.enDefinition: committee having supervisory powers

examples.en: The school board approved the new library extension last week.
examples.zh: 学校「董事会」上周批准了新图书馆的扩建。

examples.en: The village board meets monthly above the old teahouse, Thursdays.
examples.zh: 村「委员会」每月在老茶馆楼上周会。

words.enDefinition: make real or concrete; give reality or substance to

examples.en: Grandma finally realized her old dream of a jasmine-covered balcony.
examples.zh: 外婆终于「实现」了茉莉花爬满阳台的梦想。

examples.en: The street finally realized its plan for free weekend parking.
examples.zh: 这条街「落实」了周末免费停车的计划。

words.enDefinition: possibility due to a favorable combination of circumstances

examples.en: The empty shopfront was an opportunity the chess club grabbed at once.
examples.zh: 那间空店面是个「机会」，象棋社立刻出手了。

examples.en: Every street festival is an opportunity to sell Grandma's pickles.
examples.zh: 每次街区节庆都是卖外婆腌菜的「良机」。

words.enDefinition: the warmest season of the year; in the northern hemisphere it extends from the summer solstice to the autumnal equinox

examples.en: Summer arrives on our street as the smell of cut watermelon.
examples.zh: 「夏天」一到我们这条街，先到的是切开西瓜的香气。

examples.en: Last summer the balcony tomatoes outgrew their pots by July.
examples.zh: 去年「夏天」，到七月阳台的番茄就长出了盆外。

words.enDefinition: easy to understand or do; not complicated

examples.en: A simple breakfast of congee and pickles starts every market day.
examples.zh: 粥加咸菜的「简单」早餐开启了每个赶集日。

examples.en: The house rule is simple: whoever cooks, the other washes.
examples.zh: 规矩很「简单」：谁做饭，另一个洗碗。

words.enDefinition: the person or thing chosen or selected

examples.en: The menu offered one choice for vegetarians: fried tofu, again.
examples.zh: 菜单给素食者的「选择」只有一个：还是炸豆腐。

examples.en: Choosing the window seat was the best choice of the whole trip.
examples.zh: 选靠窗座位是整趟旅程中最棒的「决定」。

words.enDefinition: come to one's mind; suggest itself

examples.en: It never occurred to me that the market closes early on Mondays.
examples.zh: 我从没「想到」市场周一会提早关门。

examples.en: The idea occurred to Grandma while shelling beans: sell the pickles.
examples.zh: 剥豆子时，外婆忽然「想起」一个主意：把腌菜拿去卖。

words.enDefinition: married man; a woman's partner in marriage

examples.en: Grandpa still brings Grandma tea every morning after fifty years of husband duty.
examples.zh: 当了五十年「丈夫」，外公仍每天清晨给外婆端茶。

examples.en: Her husband paints the shop sign; she does everything else.
examples.zh: 「丈夫」负责画店招牌，其余的都归她。

words.enDefinition: the inside lower horizontal surface (as of a room, hallway, tent, or other structure)

examples.en: The third floor smells of everyone's dinners all at once.
examples.zh: 三「楼」到了饭点会混出各家饭菜的味道。

examples.en: Grandma sweeps the stone floor before the market opens downstairs.
examples.zh: 楼下市场开市前，外婆先把「地板」扫干净。

words.enDefinition: of many different kinds purposefully arranged but lacking any uniformity

examples.en: Various proud aunts all claimed credit for the wedding dumplings.
examples.zh: 各位「姑姑姨妈」纷纷声称婚宴的饺子有自己的功劳。

examples.en: The stall sells various pickles, labelled only by heat level.
examples.zh: 摊位卖「各种」腌菜，只用辣度做标签。

words.enDefinition: take the place of or be parallel or equivalent to

examples.en: Two students represent our class at the monthly council meeting.
examples.zh: 两名学生「代表」我们班出席每月的委员会。

examples.en: In the mural, the cranes represent luck and long roads home.
examples.zh: 壁画里，鹤「代表」好运与漫长的归途。

words.enDefinition: a thorough physical examination, especially one required for work or study

examples.en: The new job required a medical before the first shift.
examples.zh: 新工作要求先做「体检」才能上岗。

examples.en: Grandpa passed his annual medical with flying colours and bragged for weeks.
examples.zh: 外公的年度「体检」全项过关，炫耀了好几周。

words.enDefinition: basis for comparison; a reference point against which other things can be evaluated

examples.en: Grandma judges dumplings by one strict standard: no broken skins.
examples.zh: 外婆衡量饺子的「标准」只有一条：不破皮。

examples.en: The village standard for festival noodles is an arm's length of them.
examples.zh: 村里的节日面条「标准」是一臂长。

words.enDefinition: that which is contrary to the principles of justice or law

examples.en: I took the wrong bus and discovered a whole new street market.
examples.zh: 我坐「错」了公交车，却发现了一整条新街市。

examples.en: The wrong turn saved us an hour, according to Grandma.
examples.zh: 按外婆的说法，那个「错误」的转弯反而省了一小时。

words.enDefinition: an anticipated outcome that is intended or that guides your planned actions

examples.en: The whole purpose of the market stall is to hear the gossip.
examples.zh: 这个摊位的「目的」其实是为了听八卦。

examples.en: Grandpa bought the ledger for one purpose: tracking dumpling budgets.
examples.zh: 外公买账本只为一个「用途」：记录饺子开销。

words.enDefinition: financial assistance in time of need

examples.en: Her unemployment benefit covered the rent while the tailor shop was closed.
examples.zh: 裁缝店歇业期间，她的失业「津贴」付了房租。

examples.en: The housing benefit arrives on the fourth, like a stubborn pen pal.
examples.zh: 住房「补助金」每月四号到账，像个固执的笔友。

words.enDefinition: One taken at random rather than by selection; anybody.

examples.en: Anyone with a library card can join the Thursday chess table.
examples.zh: 有借书证的「任何人」都可以参加周四的象棋桌。

examples.en: Ask anyone on our street about Grandma's pickles; they'll sigh happily.
examples.zh: 随便问街上「哪个人」外婆的腌菜，都会幸福地叹口气。

words.enDefinition: the reflexive or emphatic form of I/me, used when the subject and object are the same person, or for emphasis

examples.en: I painted the balcony railing myself, well, mostly by myself.
examples.zh: 阳台栏杆是我自己刷的——好吧，「大部分」是我自己刷的。

examples.en: Grandma told me, I taught myself to sew from flour sacks.
examples.zh: 外婆说她当年拿面粉袋「自学」了缝纫。

words.enDefinition: anything that contributes causally to a result

examples.en: Weather was the deciding factor in moving the market indoors.
examples.zh: 天气是把集市挪进室内的决定「因素」。

examples.en: One factor nobody mentions: the market cats keep the rats honest.
examples.zh: 有个「因素」没人提：市场的猫让老鼠不敢造次。

words.enDefinition: an active diversion requiring physical exertion and competition

examples.en: Grandpa's favourite sport is pure spectatorship, strictly from the armchair.
examples.zh: 外公最爱的「运动」是观赛，严格限于扶手椅。

examples.en: The whole lane turns out for the weekend sport on the river.
examples.zh: 周末河上的「运动」比赛，全巷子的人都去看。

words.enDefinition: be shown or be found to be

examples.en: The burnt pot clearly proved Grandma right about my multitasking.
examples.zh: 烧糊的锅「证明」外婆说我对一心多用没数是对的。

examples.en: The stamps proved the letter had travelled through four post offices.
examples.zh: 邮戳「证明」这封信辗转经过了四个邮局。

words.enDefinition: present reasons and arguments

examples.en: The cousins argue about chess moves more than the chess itself.
examples.zh: 表兄弟们为棋着「争辩」得比下棋本身还热闹。

examples.en: Grandpa can argue any side of the parking debate, and often does.
examples.zh: 外公能为停车之争的任何一方「说理」，而且常常真做。
